states.content: Cardioversion remains the plan for Marcus Reed's atrial fibrillation rhythm control. The Wednesday, March 11 slot was released; the new tentative procedure slot is Thursday, March 12 at 11:10 AM with 9:40 AM arrival. Marcus requests that the procedure slot details be put in the chart. Dr. Patel has reviewed the labs and stated they are acceptable for outpatient cardioversion, satisfying the pending-labs condition; full medication history reconciliation remains part of the plan. Dr. Patel instructs that Marcus must not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion. Pharmacist Klein confirms apixaban stays at 5 mg twice daily and Marcus must not stop or skip it on his own unless the cardiologist specifically says otherwise. The only routine periprocedural hold discussed is lisinopril on the morning of the procedure once the date is confirmed. Nurse Jamison will bring Marcus back first for his cardiology rhythm clinic visit, and Nina can be updated on arrival windows if Marcus keeps the logistics-only setting active.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: Nurse Jamison is reviewing Marcus Reed's medications exactly as he is taking them right now, to prepare an accurate current medication list. Marcus reported taking ibuprofen a couple of times last week for shoulder pain before remembering he probably should not with the blood thinner (apixaban). Dr. Patel has now instructed Marcus to stop ibuprofen and other NSAIDs and to use acetaminophen instead if needed, because NSAIDs raise bleeding risk with apixaban. Pharmacist Klein reinforced this: no ibuprofen or naproxen while Marcus is on apixaban. Marcus reported he has not missed any morning apixaban doses and no completely missed doses in the last three weeks as far as he remembers; he might have been a few hours late last Monday night when changing locations but still took that pill before bed. Marcus is pretty sure he took his Monday-night apixaban dose, but it was late and he cannot prove the time. Nurse Jamison will document the Monday-night apixaban dose as possibly delayed but not skipped. Marcus does not drink energy drinks.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: Marcus Reed's current medication regimen: apixaban 5 mg twice daily without interruption; he must not stop or skip apixaban on his own, and it stays at 5 mg twice daily unless the cardiologist specifically says otherwise. Metoprolol tartrate increased from 25 mg to 37.5 mg twice daily starting tonight (using 25-mg tablets, this is one and a half tablets in the morning and one and a half tablets in the evening). Lisinopril 10 mg daily (hold morning dose on procedure day once date finalized). Omeprazole 20 mg daily. Dr. Patel instructed him to stop ibuprofen and other NSAIDs and use acetaminophen instead if needed, and to start magnesium oxide 400 mg nightly for five nights because his previous magnesium trend has been low-normal. Pharmacist Klein reinforced: magnesium oxide 400 mg nightly for five nights, and no ibuprofen or naproxen while on apixaban.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: Over the past week Marcus Reed has had chest fluttering most evenings, shortness of breath climbing stairs, and one episode of lightheadedness on Saturday; he did not pass out. He also reports no chest pain and no bleeding, but has a racing heartbeat and feels washed out. His presentation is characterized as symptomatic atrial fibrillation/flutter with exertional dyspnea and lightheadedness, and no active bleeding. Clinician Dr. Patel confirms he is still in atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response but is stable enough for an outpatient rhythm-control plan. He had shoulder pain last week, for which he took ibuprofen a couple of times before remembering he probably should not with the blood thinner.
